      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Agenda

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Ordinary Council Meeting

      Tuesday, February 27, 2024 - 06:00 PM

      Agenda

      Agenda (7.63 MB)

      Minutes

      Minutes (635.03 KB)

      Attachments

      Minutes (143.22 MB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      astc@astc.nt.gov.au

      (08) 8950 0500

      (08) 8953 0558

      PO Box 1071 Alice Springs NT 0871

      Hours & Location

      93 Todd Street Alice Springs NT 0870

      Monday to Friday 8am - 5pm

      Follow Us

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Ordinary Council Meeting - 26 September 2023

      Tuesday, September 26, 2023 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (9.63 MB)

      Minutes

      Minutes.pdf (350.64 KB)

      Attachments

      Audio.mp3 (91.95 MB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      astc@astc.nt.gov.au

      (08) 8950 0500

      (08) 8953 0558

      PO Box 1071 Alice Springs NT 0871

      Hours & Location

      93 Todd Street Alice Springs NT 0870

      Monday to Friday 8am - 5pm

      Follow Us

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Ordinary Council Meeting - 26 April 2023

      Wednesday, April 26, 2023 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (3.82 MB)

      Minutes

      Minutes.pdf (291.85 KB)

      Attachments

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Ordinary Council Meeting - 27 September 2022

      Tuesday, September 27, 2022 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (29.94 MB)

      Minutes

      Minutes.pdf (241.80 KB)

      Attachments

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Ordinary Council Meeting - 29 June 2022

      Wednesday, June 29, 2022 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (24.50 MB)

      Minutes

      Minutes.pdf (241.70 KB)

      Attachments

      Audio.mp3 (97.52 MB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      astc@astc.nt.gov.au

      (08) 8950 0500

      (08) 8953 0558

      PO Box 1071 Alice Springs NT 0871

      Hours & Location

      93 Todd Street Alice Springs NT 0870

      Monday to Friday 8am - 5pm

      Follow Us

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Ordinary Council Meeting - 25 January 2022

      Tuesday, January 25, 2022 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (13.30 MB)

      Minutes

      Minutes.pdf (225.32 KB)

      Attachments

      Audio.mp3 (223.17 MB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Ordinary Council Meeting - 14 December 2021

      Tuesday, December 14, 2021 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (52.40 MB)

      Minutes

      Minutes.pdf (359.19 KB)

      Attachments

      Audio.mp3 (180.70 MB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      astc@astc.nt.gov.au

      (08) 8953 0558

      PO Box 1071 Alice Springs NT 0871

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Tuesday, July 13, 2021 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Ordinary Council Meeting - 28 April 2021

      Wednesday, April 28, 2021 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (4.56 MB)

      Minutes

      Minutes.pdf (192.75 KB)

      Attachments

      Audio.mp3 (151.49 MB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Ordinary Council Meeting - 09 March 2021

      Tuesday, March 9, 2021 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (4.96 MB)

      Minutes

      UNCONFIRMED - Minutes.pdf (274.23 KB)

      Minutes.pdf (212.27 KB)

      Attachments

      Audio.mp3 (43.14 MB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      astc@astc.nt.gov.au

      (08) 8950 0500

      (08) 8953 0558

      PO Box 1071 Alice Springs NT 0871

      Hours & Location

      93 Todd Street Alice Springs NT 0870

      Monday to Friday 8am - 5pm

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Ordinary Council Meeting - 09 February 2021

      Tuesday, February 9, 2021 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (2.49 MB)

      Minutes

      Minutes.pdf (152.96 KB)

      Attachments

      Audio.mp3 (27.17 MB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Special Council Meeting - 29 November 2021

      Monday, November 29, 2021 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (298.84 KB)

      Minutes

      Minutes.pdf (87.04 KB)

      Attachments

      Audio.mp3 (7.60 MB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      astc@astc.nt.gov.au

      (08) 8950 0500

      (08) 8953 0558

      PO Box 1071 Alice Springs NT 0871

      Hours & Location

      93 Todd Street Alice Springs NT 0870

      Monday to Friday 8am - 5pm

      Follow Us

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Ordinary Council Meeting - 08 December 2020

      Tuesday, December 8, 2020 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (54.11 MB)

      Minutes

      Minutes.pdf (193.32 KB)

      Attachments

      Audio.mp3 (156.67 MB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Ordinary Council Meeting - 29 September 2020

      Tuesday, September 29, 2020 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (9.71 MB)

      Minutes

      UNCONFIRMED - Minutes.pdf (421.99 KB)

      Minutes.pdf (342.51 KB)

      Attachments

      Audio.mp3 (155.76 MB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      astc@astc.nt.gov.au

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights.       Special Council Meeting - 23 December 2020

      Wednesday, December 23, 2020 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (227.14 KB)

      Minutes

      Minutes.pdf (111.11 KB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Special Council Meeting - 04 May 2020

      Monday, May 4, 2020 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (1.19 MB)

      Minutes

      UNCONFIRMED - Minutes.pdf (326.17 KB)

      Minutes.pdf (256.66 KB)

      Attachments

      Audio.mp3 (176.85 MB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      astc@astc.nt.gov.au

      (08) 8950 0500

      (08) 8953 0558

      PO Box 1071 Alice Springs NT 0871

      Hours & Location

      93 Todd Street Alice Springs NT 0870

      Monday to Friday 8am - 5pm

      Follow Us

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Special Confidential Meeting - 09 April 2024

      Tuesday, April 9, 2024 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (295.32 KB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      astc@astc.nt.gov.au

      (08) 8950 0500

      (08) 8953 0558

      PO Box 1071 Alice Springs NT 0871

      Hours & Location

      93 Todd Street Alice Springs NT 0870

      Monday to Friday 8am - 5pm

      Follow Us

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Special Confidential Meeting - 18 May 2023

      Thursday, May 18, 2023 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (248.70 KB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      astc@astc.nt.gov.au

      (08) 8950 0500

      (08) 8953 0558

      PO Box 1071 Alice Springs NT 0871

      Hours & Location

      93 Todd Street Alice Springs NT 0870

      Monday to Friday 8am - 5pm

      Follow Us

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Special Confidential Meeting - 21 February 2023

      Tuesday, February 21, 2023 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (247.27 KB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      astc@astc.nt.gov.au

      (08) 8950 0500

      (08) 8953 0558

      PO Box 1071 Alice Springs NT 0871

      Hours & Location

      93 Todd Street Alice Springs NT 0870

      Monday to Friday 8am - 5pm

      Follow Us

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Special Confidential Meeting - 20 May 2022

      Friday, May 20, 2022 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (225.72 KB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      astc@astc.nt.gov.au

      (08) 8950 0500

      (08) 8953 0558

      PO Box 1071 Alice Springs NT 0871

      Hours & Location

      93 Todd Street Alice Springs NT 0870

      Monday to Friday 8am - 5pm

      Follow Us

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Special Confidential Meeting - 21 December 2021

      Tuesday, December 21, 2021 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (298.53 KB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Contact Us

      astc@astc.nt.gov.au

      (08) 8950 0500

      (08) 8953 0558

      PO Box 1071 Alice Springs NT 0871

      Hours & Location

      93 Todd Street Alice Springs NT 0870

      Monday to Friday 8am - 5pm

      Follow Us

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Development Committee Meeting - 07 June 2021

      Monday, June 7, 2021 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (124.81 KB)

      Minutes

      UNCONFIRMED - Minutes.pdf (195.77 KB)

      Minutes.pdf (164.86 KB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Tuesday, April 6, 2021 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (126.00 KB)

      Minutes

      UNCONFIRMED - Minutes.pdf (190.53 KB)

      Minutes.pdf (190.42 KB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Development Committee Meeting - 07 December 2020

      Monday, December 7, 2020 - 12:00 AM

      Agenda

      Agenda.pdf (129.13 KB)

      Minutes

      UNCONFIRMED - Minutes.pdf (199.30 KB)

      Minutes.pdf (165.28 KB)

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present, and celebrate a deep and ongoing connection to this land, its waters, and its stories. We endeavour to listen, learn and grow as we continue our ongoing journey towards reconciliation.

      Universal Declaration of Human Rights

      Alice Springs Town Council is committed to the fundamental principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in which all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Humans are inherent with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of common humanity, without distinction of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

      Council acknowledges the Central Arrernte people as the Traditional Owners of Mparntwe, the Country where we live and work.
